description: Boston University’s undergraduate program in African American & Black Diaspora Studies, housed in the College of Arts & Sciences, focuses on the history, culture, and politics of people of African descent throughout the world. The curriculum encourages students to explore how race and racialization have shaped institutions and social relations, both historically and in the contemporary moment. Students are provided with critical tools to study Black history, cultures, and societies in a global context, with particular attention to transnational connections among African peoples across the diaspora. Our multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach combines the rigor of humanities and social science disciplines to promote critical thinking, advanced research, and written and oral communication skills relevant to a diverse range of post-graduate pursuits. Majors in African American & Black Diaspora Studies are well prepared for careers in fields such as law, medicine, education, journalism, public policy, community organizing, and the arts, as well as for further graduate study across the humanities and social sciences.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in African American & Black Diaspora Studies

description: Boston University’s Minor in African Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give undergraduates a broad knowledge of Africa and to allow them to focus on a particular discipline or area of interest. Students take a combination of required and elective courses from a range of disciplines offered by various departments and schools across the University, including courses on the history, politics, societies, cultures, religions, and arts of Africa, as well as several African languages. Students may also pursue study abroad in Africa, or participate in the African Studies Center’s internship program in Africa or the African diaspora. These experiences are highly recommended for the Minor in African Studies.
Program name: Minor in African Studies

description: The American Studies major focuses on the United States and its place in the world, with particular attention to how ideas of America and American-ness have been produced, challenged, and transformed from the colonial period to the present. The program offers students an interdisciplinary approach to studying the United States, drawing on insights and methods from across the humanities and social sciences. Students are encouraged to develop their own critical perspectives on American culture, society, and history, and to cultivate the skills necessary to engage in public discourse about the past, present, and future of the nation. The American Studies program cultivates critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and effective communication—skills that are highly valued in a wide range of professions. Graduates pursue careers in fields such as law, journalism, public policy, education, museum studies, and nonprofit management. Many also go on to graduate school in history, literature, or other related disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in American Studies

description: Boston University’s undergraduate major in Anthropology (BA) provides students with a broad and rigorous exposure to the core subfields of anthropology – sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, and biological anthropology – and an appreciation of their historical development, theoretical foundations, and methodological approaches. Our curriculum emphasizes the dynamic interconnections among these subfields as they explore the range of human experience and behavior, past and present, in socio-cultural, biological, and archaeological contexts. Students are encouraged to develop a deeper understanding of anthropology through hands-on research opportunities and field programs both in Boston and abroad (e.g., our summer archaeological field school, field research in Ecuador, and other opportunities offered through the Boston University Study Abroad program). Beyond the classroom, our students have engaged in a wide range of internship opportunities at such places as the Peabody Essex Museum, the Museum of Fine Arts, the Boston Children’s Museum, local archaeological firms, and cultural organizations that serve Boston’s diverse immigrant communities. Anthropology majors also pursue diverse career paths after graduation, including medicine and public health, international relations, social justice and advocacy, museum work, and academia, among many others. The BA program in Anthropology thus provides students with the intellectual tools for understanding a complex and interconnected world and the skills that are increasingly valued by employers in a globalized society.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology

description: Archaeology at Boston University is a distinct interdisciplinary program designed to give students a global and multicultural perspective on societies, both ancient and recent. Our faculty specializes in the archaeology of Europe, the Mediterranean, the Near East, Mesoamerica, and North America. Archaeology BA students master the foundational theories, methodologies, and ethics of archaeology, as well as the history, ecology, and social organization of past human societies. The BA program provides excellent preparation for further study in graduate school or for careers in related fields such as cultural resource management, museums, education, or historical preservation.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Archaeology

description: Asian Studies at Boston University offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate major that addresses the histories, cultures, politics, and societies of Asia. Students gain critical insight into the diverse regions of East Asia (China, Japan, Korea) and South/Southeast Asia (India, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, etc.), and they develop expertise in at least one Asian language. The program emphasizes a holistic approach, encouraging students to explore Asia from multiple disciplinary perspectives, including history, political science, anthropology, religion, and literature. Graduates are prepared for careers in government, international relations, journalism, education, business, and further graduate study, equipped with strong analytical skills, cross-cultural competence, and deep knowledge of one of the world’s most dynamic and influential continents.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Asian Studies

description: As an astronomy student in BU’s College of Arts & Sciences (CAS), you’ll explore the vast, evolving universe through a challenging curriculum of physics, mathematics, and astronomy courses. You’ll be encouraged to get involved in research with faculty in areas such as observational and theoretical astrophysics, planetary science, solar physics, and instrumentation. Astronomy majors develop strong quantitative and analytical skills that serve them well, not only in graduate school, but in a wide variety of careers including science education, science policy, data science, and scientific computing. A BA in Astronomy is a good choice for students interested in a broad liberal arts education, or those wishing to combine their study of astronomy with a second major.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Astronomy

description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Biology provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the biological sciences, a mastery of basic research skills, and an appreciation of the social and ethical aspects of biology. The BA program is designed for students who want a strong foundation in biology, but also wish to have the flexibility to pursue other academic interests, such as a second major or minor, or pre-professional studies outside of the sciences. The BA in Biology prepares students for careers in diverse fields such as medicine, dentistry, public health, law, business, education, and science writing. It also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in biology or related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Biology
Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

description: The Department of Chemistry offers two undergraduate degrees: a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Chemistry and a Bachelor of Science (BS) in Chemistry. Both degrees provide a strong background in the major areas of chemistry. The BS degree is more intensive, designed for students who are preparing for a career in chemistry or related fields, or for graduate study in chemistry. Students are encouraged to participate in research with faculty members in Chemistry, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, or other departments. Opportunities for research include during the academic year, the summer, and a semester in BU’s study abroad program in Dresden, Germany.
Accreditation status: Certified by the American Chemical Society.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Chemistry

description: The BA in Cinema & Media Studies offers students a critical and theoretical understanding of moving images and screen cultures across different media platforms, historical periods, and national contexts. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including the history of cinema, television studies, digital media, critical theory, and the political economy of media industries. Students develop analytical skills to interpret and evaluate cinematic and media texts, explore the social, cultural, and political impact of media, and engage with contemporary debates in the field. The program prepares students for various careers in media industries, arts and culture organizations, education, and graduate studies in cinema and media studies or related humanities fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Cinema & Media Studies

description: A deep investigation of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds through their material and literary cultures, with a focus on historical study. Students pursuing a BA in Classical Studies with a concentration in Classical Archaeology explore archaeology, art history, history, languages, literature, and culture from the Bronze Age through Late Antiquity. This concentration combines archaeological fieldwork, museum studies, and advanced study in art history and history with intensive language training and literary studies. Students engage with the intellectual, political, and social history of the classical world and its material remains from the Mediterranean and Near East.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies

description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Computer Science in the College of Arts & Sciences provides students with a broad education in the liberal arts and a major in computer science. The program trains students in the fundamental principles and practical applications of computing while allowing them to develop expertise in other subjects and explore new interests. A major in computer science provides students with an education in the principles and applications of computing. Through coursework, students develop the skills needed to design, implement, and analyze computational solutions to problems across a range of applications. The BA program provides a robust foundation in computer science and also allows students to pursue interests in other fields by giving them greater flexibility in their curriculum.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science

description: The BU Core Curriculum offers a unique opportunity to engage with many of Boston University’s best teachers, explore timeless questions about justice, truth, good, and evil, and form close intellectual relationships with other students. The Core minor allows students to earn minor credit for work they are already doing in the Core or to extend their Core experience beyond the four-semester sequence.
Program name: Minor in Core Curriculum

description: The Core Curriculum is designed to broaden students’ intellectual horizons, introduce them to major fields of inquiry, and foster an appreciation of the enduring questions of human existence. The Core offers an interdisciplinary approach to the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences through team-taught courses and a cohort-based experience for the first two years. A minor in Core Independent Studies requires a minimum of five (5) courses (20 credits) and is open to all students at Boston University.
Program name: Minor in Core Independent Studies

description: Our BA in Earth & Environment program offers students a broad interdisciplinary training in earth and environmental sciences and their interaction with human society. Graduates are prepared for a variety of professions in fields such as environmental consulting, environmental law, city and regional planning, natural resource management, and environmental education. Many graduates also pursue advanced degrees in these fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Earth & Environment

description: As a student pursuing a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Economics, you will become fluent in the tools of economic analysis and develop the quantitative reasoning and data analysis skills increasingly valued in a broad range of occupations. You will learn to apply economic reasoning to analyze and understand social behavior, evaluate public policy, and make sound decisions in business and finance. The BA in Economics provides a strong foundation for employment in business, finance, consulting, and government, and for graduate study in law, business, and public policy, as well as economics.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Economics

description: The Department of English offers a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree program that emphasizes critical thinking, close reading, and effective communication through the study of literature. Students explore a wide range of literary periods, genres, and theoretical approaches, developing skills in analysis, interpretation, and persuasive writing. Our curriculum is designed to foster a deep understanding of literary history and cultural contexts, while also encouraging students to engage with contemporary literary debates and creative practices. Graduates are well-prepared for careers in fields such as education, publishing, journalism, law, marketing, and public relations, or for continued graduate study.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in English

Concentration name: German Studies and Russian & East European Studies
description: The BA in European Studies offers students an interdisciplinary liberal arts education that focuses on the cultures, economies, history, politics, and languages of Europe. The program draws on faculty and courses in the Departments of Classical Studies, Economics, History, Modern Languages & Comparative Literature, Political Science, and Philosophy, as well as the Pardee School of Global Studies. Students achieve proficiency in an official European language and write a capstone senior thesis. Students choose a concentration in either German Studies or Russian & East European Studies.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in European Studies

description: Global Medieval Studies (GMS) is a truly interdisciplinary program that approaches the Middle Ages not as a 'dark age' between two golden ages, but rather as an exciting and formative period of global history. Our program brings together faculty from across Boston University to offer courses that highlight the interconnectedness of different world regions—from Europe and the Mediterranean to Africa, Asia, and the Americas—during the premodern era (roughly 500-1500 CE). In our courses, students explore the cultures, societies, religions, politics, and environments of the global Middle Ages. Students learn to critically analyze various primary sources (texts, artifacts, images, music) and engage with diverse methodologies from different disciplines (history, art history, literature, musicology, religion, philosophy, archaeology, etc.). Through their studies, students develop strong analytical, research, and communication skills applicable to a wide range of careers.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Global Medieval Studies

description: The Department of History emphasizes historical analysis and research skills, enabling students to evaluate arguments, weigh evidence, analyze problems, and craft persuasive arguments. Students gain a deep understanding of historical forces that have shaped the contemporary world, and they develop capacities for critical analysis, research, and communication that are applicable to a wide range of careers. History majors at BU develop: A deep understanding of the historical forces that have shaped the contemporary world; A capacity for critical historical analysis and research across different periods and cultures; The ability to evaluate arguments, weigh evidence, analyze problems, and craft persuasive arguments; and Skills in research, critical thinking, and communication that prepare them for a diverse range of careers.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in History

description: Art history provides insight into the history of human culture. Courses address issues of aesthetics, meaning, function, patronage, conservation, and display in the visual arts, as well as the history of architecture and urbanism around the world. As a discipline, art history engages with areas ranging from anthropology to computer science. Our students develop visual, historical, and critical literacy and the communication and research skills necessary to pursue a wide array of careers in the arts and beyond. Through the study of art and architecture, students cultivate a global perspective, a critical understanding of both historical and contemporary societies, and an appreciation for the impact of cultural heritage.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in History of Art & Architecture

description: Boston University’s interdisciplinary Holocaust, Genocide & Human Rights Studies (HGHRS) major provides students with the critical tools necessary to analyze, understand, and respond to mass atrocities and violations of human rights across the globe. The program offers a unique opportunity for students to engage with diverse disciplinary perspectives—including history, political science, sociology, anthropology, literature, religion, and law—on genocide and human rights through a rigorous course of study grounded in historical and comparative analysis. Students in the HGHRS major will develop strong analytical skills, hone their research and writing abilities, and cultivate an ethically informed understanding of the political, social, and cultural challenges posed by contemporary human rights struggles. Graduates of the program will be well-prepared for a range of careers in law, public policy, education, human rights advocacy, social justice, and international affairs.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Holocaust, Genocide & Human Rights Studies

description: International relations is a dynamic interdisciplinary field that helps students understand the evolution of the modern global system. Drawing on courses in political science, economics, history, and other disciplines, the IR program at BU provides students with the analytical tools and substantive knowledge necessary to comprehend critical global issues and foreign policy processes. The program also offers students the opportunity to conduct faculty-mentored research, to study abroad at BU’s international centers, and to participate in a vibrant community of faculty and students. The Pardee School of Global Studies offers students a multidisciplinary education in global affairs, integrating social science, regional and thematic studies, and foreign languages. Our IR program is one leading example of this approach, offering a broad curriculum built around a core of political science, economics, and history. Our graduates gain valuable analytical skills for careers in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. Many go on to graduate study, including law school.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in International Relations

description: Students pursuing the Minor in Israel Studies are expected to choose courses across different departments that relate to modern Israel (since the 19th century). The minor is open to students in all colleges and schools within Boston University. By pursuing a Minor in Israel Studies, students will explore the society, politics, history, religion, and culture of Israel in a multidisciplinary fashion.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Israel Studies

description: The BA in Jewish Studies offers students the opportunity to study the history, culture, religion, and languages of the Jewish people from antiquity to the present. The program is inherently interdisciplinary, drawing on courses in Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations, Religion, History, English, Philosophy, and other departments and programs. Students are exposed to the wide variety of scholarly approaches that characterize the field of Jewish Studies. Required courses introduce students to foundational texts, historical periods, and methodologies of the discipline. Our students are required to master Hebrew (or another Jewish language such as Yiddish) through the intermediate level, which provides them access to primary texts in their original languages. Small classes facilitate lively engagement with course material and close interaction with faculty. Our students cultivate critical thinking, textual analysis, and communication skills through the curriculum and produce a substantial senior essay. Students are encouraged to study abroad in Israel or other centers of Jewish life, and many elect to do so during their junior year. Graduates of the program are well prepared for careers in education, public service, communal work, and the rabbinate, and for advanced study in Jewish Studies and related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Jewish Studies

description: The Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on courses offered in the departments of Anthropology, History, International Relations, Modern Languages & Comparative Literature, Political Science, and Sociology. Courses include the study of history, economics, politics, anthropology, sociology, and the literatures and cultures of the region. The BA in Latin American Studies provides students with a multidisciplinary understanding of the Latin American region. Students will study its history, economy, political systems, anthropology, and sociology, as well as its rich literature and diverse cultures. It requires coursework in various fields, with a particular focus on the humanities and social sciences. The program encourages students to complete a study abroad experience in a Latin American country. Students should complete language proficiency requirements in Spanish, Portuguese, or Haitian Creole by their junior year. Graduates are prepared for a wide variety of career paths in both the private and public sectors, including business, foreign service, journalism, research, and law. Many graduates go on to pursue advanced degrees in Latin American studies or related fields.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American Studies

description:
Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. Linguistics majors at Boston University develop a thorough understanding of the scientific investigation of linguistic systems. The Department of Linguistics at Boston University is a vibrant, productive, and congenial intellectual community that offers a highly ranked doctoral program as well as successful undergraduate programs in Linguistics and in Computer Science & Linguistics. Students have many opportunities to conduct research with faculty and engage with the wider linguistic community through presentations, workshops, and colloquia. BU’s Linguistics majors are prepared for graduate study in linguistics, cognitive science, computational linguistics, or language documentation, as well as for careers in software development, computational linguistics, education, government, and other fields. The major also provides a solid foundation for careers in law, medicine, or journalism.

The BA in Linguistics is offered through the College of Arts & Sciences.

For specific requirements, please consult the Undergraduate Bulletin.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Linguistics

description: Students can pursue a BA in Latin concurrently with an MFA in Literary Translation from Boston University’s Department of Romance Studies. This dual-degree program offers an opportunity to combine the study of Latin language and literature with training in the theory and practice of literary translation. This is an accelerated, five-year program which combines the requirements of the two degrees, giving students the opportunity to earn both a Bachelor’s and a Master’s degree in a shorter timeframe than it would take to earn each degree sequentially. Upon completion of the dual degree, students will have gained a thorough knowledge of Latin literature and the ability to translate it effectively, as well as a grounding in the theory and practice of literary translation more generally. They will be prepared to enter the literary publishing world, to continue on to a PhD program in Classics or Comparative Literature, or to pursue careers in a variety of fields, including education and international relations.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Literary Translation

description: The BA in Marine Science provides students with a strong interdisciplinary understanding of the marine environment. Students pursuing a BA in Marine Science are prepared for graduate school and careers in government agencies, non-profit organizations, the private sector, and environmental education. Marine Science students have access to Boston University’s world-class faculty, research facilities, and the Boston University Marine Program (BUMP) based at our coastal field station in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Marine Science

description: This major is designed to provide students with broad exposure to both Mathematics and Statistics. It emphasizes how the two disciplines connect and offers students an opportunity to take courses in several different areas in both fields. The degree is particularly suitable for students who wish to pursue careers that utilize mathematical and statistical thinking. These include areas in finance, economics, business, medicine and the social sciences. The degree also provides a solid background for students interested in graduate studies in either mathematics or statistics.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Mathematics & Statistics

description: Middle East & North Africa Studies (MENA) is an interdisciplinary program, administered by the Pardee School of Global Studies and based in the College of Arts & Sciences. MENA Studies offers a comprehensive program of study that develops students’ understanding of the region’s languages, cultures, religions, politics, and history. Students gain a critical perspective on the political, economic, social, and cultural challenges faced by the region today. Many MENA Studies courses count towards divisional studies and general education requirements. The MENA Studies major can be combined with other majors for students to acquire expertise in a field of study and a region of the world. Students may combine MENA with other majors, such as Political Science, International Relations, Business Administration, or History. Students are encouraged to pursue internships and study abroad opportunities.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Middle East & North Africa Studies

description: Students pursuing a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in Muslim Studies complete a range of courses designed to introduce them to the diversity and complexity of Muslim cultures and societies across history and in the contemporary world. Muslim Studies is an interdisciplinary program covering the history, literature, languages, religions, political systems, arts, and cultures of Muslims from around the world. It provides students with critical perspectives and analytic tools to address current global challenges that involve Muslims and Muslim societies. The program draws on faculty from several departments across Boston University, including Anthropology, History, International Relations, Modern Languages & Comparative Literature, Political Science, Religion, and Sociology. Students are expected to complete 12 courses (48 credits) over five semesters including two courses from each of the three subject areas (History, Religion, and Society and Culture) and one additional course in Muslim Studies. They will also need to demonstrate proficiency in a relevant language.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Muslim Studies

description: Neuroscience is an interdisciplinary field that studies the nervous system and its impact on behavior and cognitive functions. Students in the Undergraduate Program in Neuroscience (UPN) explore the brain from multiple perspectives, from molecular and cellular mechanisms to systems and cognitive processes. They learn about the latest research findings, experimental techniques, and computational approaches used to understand the nervous system. The program provides a strong foundation in neuroscience principles and research methods, preparing students for careers in research, healthcare, biotechnology, and other related fields. The Bachelor of Arts in Neuroscience is a less prescriptive degree that provides students with more flexibility to combine Neuroscience with other interests such as the humanities, social sciences, or arts.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Neuroscience

description: The Department of Philosophy at Boston University is a thriving community of scholars, teachers, and students. Our internationally renowned faculty offer a wide range of courses in the history of philosophy and in contemporary analytical, Continental, and American philosophy, as well as in areas of value theory (ethics, aesthetics, political philosophy) and the philosophy of language, mind, and science. The department emphasizes a pluralistic approach to the discipline, fostering openness to a wide array of views and approaches. Students majoring in philosophy at Boston University develop strong analytical and critical skills, as well as abilities in clear writing and precise expression. They learn to identify the presuppositions and implications of various positions, to analyze and interpret complex texts, and to construct and defend cogent arguments of their own. These skills are essential not only for graduate study in philosophy but also for law school and other professional programs, as well as for careers in virtually all fields that demand critical intelligence, creative problem-solving, and communication skills.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy

description: Physics is the study of the natural world, from the smallest subatomic particles to the largest structures in the universe. Our BA program in Physics offers a broad, flexible education for students interested in this fundamental science. As a BA Physics student, you’ll build a strong foundation in classical and quantum mechanics, electromagnetism, and thermodynamics, while also having ample opportunity to explore other interests. This program is suitable for students who want to combine their passion for physics with a second major in a field such as computer science, mathematics, chemistry, or even the humanities. The BA is also an excellent option for students planning to pursue careers in areas like science communication, education, business, law, or medicine, where an understanding of scientific principles is valuable.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Physics

description: Our BA in Political Science program offers students a rigorous and comprehensive education in the study of politics. Through a combination of core courses, electives, and opportunities for independent research, students gain a deep understanding of political institutions, processes, and behavior at local, national, and international levels. The curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, analytical skills, and effective communication, preparing students for a wide range of careers in government, law, business, journalism, non-profit organizations, and academia. Graduates of our program are equipped to analyze complex political issues, engage in informed public discourse, and contribute meaningfully to their communities and the world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science

description: Students in the BA program learn about mind and behavior, using psychological science to address real-world challenges like mental illness, social problems, and how people interact with technology. As an interdisciplinary social science degree, the BA is a popular choice for students who want to combine their passion for psychological science with other interests in the humanities, social sciences, and the arts. Our BA students go on to graduate school or professional careers in fields like public health, law, social work, business, counseling, marketing, and education. Learning Outcomes: Students will identify and describe core concepts, theories, and empirical findings in psychological and brain sciences; understand and apply various research methods in psychological and brain sciences; critically evaluate psychological and brain sciences research and theories; communicate effectively about psychological and brain sciences topics, both orally and in writing; and apply psychological and brain sciences knowledge and skills to real-world problems and ethical considerations.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Psychological & Brain Sciences

description: Our Bachelor of Arts in Religion offers students a chance to explore the major religious traditions of the world from a variety of perspectives, including historical, philosophical, sociological, literary, and anthropological approaches. The Department of Religion at Boston University offers courses in a range of religious traditions, including Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Buddhism, Hinduism, Daoism, Confucianism, and indigenous religions, as well as cross-cultural and comparative studies of religion. Students learn to critically analyze religion in its diverse forms through engagement with different theoretical and methodological frameworks. Religion majors develop strong analytical, research, and writing skills, which prepare them for a variety of careers in fields such as law, education, journalism, international relations, social work, business, and medicine, as well as for graduate study in religion and related disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Religion

description:
The BA in Romance Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to give students broad exposure to the languages, literatures, and cultures of the Romance-speaking world. The program also offers a critical theoretical perspective on the very concept of the Romance-speaking world, exploring the history of the concept, the diverse forms it takes today, and its relation to other linguistic and cultural systems. Students in the program develop a critical awareness of cultural diversity through the study of languages, literatures, and cultures such as French, Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese. They learn to analyze and interpret texts, articulate complex ideas, and engage in informed cultural critique. The Romance Studies curriculum prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as education, international relations, journalism, and cultural heritage, and for further study in graduate school.

As a result of completing the Romance Studies major, students will be able to:
* Analyze and interpret texts, discourses, and cultural practices from the Romance-speaking world, situating them within their historical, social, and cultural contexts.
* Identify and critically evaluate central issues, debates, and theories in the interdisciplinary field of Romance Studies.
* Communicate effectively in at least one Romance language other than English, and demonstrate an understanding of its grammar, syntax, and cultural nuances.
* Conduct independent research, formulate original arguments, and articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively in both written and oral forms.
* Demonstrate a critical awareness of cultural diversity and cross-cultural communication, and apply this understanding to analyze global issues and interactions.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Romance Studies

Concentration name: Biology Track, Chemistry Track, Physics Track
description: The Bachelor of Arts (BA) in Science Education program prepares students for careers as science educators in public and private schools. Students are guided to be reflective and responsive teachers with a deep understanding of subject matter and pedagogical practice. Graduates of the BA in Science Education program receive an initial license to teach high school science (grades 8–12) in Massachusetts in their chosen content area (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics). The BA in Science Education offers coursework and fieldwork that leads to an initial license to teach Biology, Chemistry, or Physics at the high school level (grades 8-12). Students are challenged to apply their growing knowledge of adolescent development, learning theory, and effective teaching practices during their coursework and through extensive field experiences, including a semester-long practicum. Field placements are arranged in local urban, suburban, and rural public high schools, allowing students to learn from a diverse range of students and faculty. All undergraduate students in Science Education must maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.75 to remain in good standing in the program. Students with a cumulative GPA below 2.75 will be placed on academic probation. If the cumulative GPA remains below 2.75 for a second consecutive semester, the student will be dismissed from the program. For further information, see the University Policy on Undergraduate Academic Standing.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Science Education

description: The BA in Sociology introduces students to the sociological perspective and helps them develop the analytic and research skills needed to understand and critically examine society, social problems, and social inequality. The major provides a solid foundation in the core areas of sociology, including social theory, research methods, and statistics. Students have the opportunity to delve into a wide array of substantive areas, such as race and ethnicity, gender, class, crime, health, environment, culture, and globalization.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Sociology

description:
Urban Studies is an interdisciplinary field that considers the complex issues that arise from human beings living in cities. The Minor in Urban Studies provides students with an understanding of urban communities and the forces that shape them, and prepares students for a range of careers and graduate work in urban planning, public policy, social work, community development, and public health.

Students completing the Minor in Urban Studies will be able to:
* Explain key issues in the study of cities and urban life in different geographical and historical contexts.
* Explain how different disciplinary approaches are used to understand urban issues.
* Formulate a research question about a current urban issue and identify appropriate methods to address it.
Program name: Urban Studies Minor

description: The Women’s, Gender & Sexuality Studies program provides students with the critical skills needed to understand how gender and sexuality shape our experiences. From understanding the historical roots of feminist thought to exploring contemporary issues like transgender rights and queer theory, you’ll engage with a diverse range of topics, developing a nuanced understanding of identity, power, and social justice. As a WGS major, you’ll cultivate interdisciplinary perspectives, honing your analytical and communication skills and preparing you to address complex challenges in a rapidly evolving world.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Women's, Gender & Sexuality Studies

description: The World Languages & Literatures major offers students the opportunity to construct an interdisciplinary degree around their interests in language, literature, and culture. Working with an advisor, students choose courses across WLL departments and CAS, and may choose to focus on a particular language, region, or topic. Students develop advanced communicative and analytical skills, the ability to think critically about texts, cultures, and societies from global perspectives, and a nuanced understanding of cultural differences. Majoring in World Languages & Literatures gives you a thorough grounding in one or more languages, literatures, and cultures through courses taken primarily within the Department of World Languages & Literatures. You develop advanced communicative and analytical skills; the ability to think critically about texts, cultures, and societies from global perspectives; and a nuanced understanding of cultural differences. As a World Languages & Literatures major, you can concentrate in a single language, or pursue the comparative track, and study a literary tradition from a range of critical perspectives while working with literary texts written in at least two languages, one of them ancient. Our majors often combine their studies with a second major or minor in another field (e.g., biology, computer science, economics, journalism, international relations, political science, history, philosophy, etc.), or study abroad for a semester or year.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in World Languages & Literatures

description: The Writing Program offers courses designed to improve students’ academic and professional writing skills through practice in analysis, interpretation, argumentation, and research. Small, discussion-based classes cultivate critical thinking and engaged inquiry; students learn to develop an argument, to understand what counts as evidence in a particular field, to respond to counterarguments, and to revise their work based on feedback from peers and instructors. Students also explore how their writing contributes to wider conversations in academic and public spheres. These courses prepare students to write effectively in their other university courses and beyond, and they are designed to support and enhance all disciplinary study. The program is home to the College of Arts & Sciences Writing Minor, which complements any major, and the Writing Center, where students can receive individualized feedback on their writing projects.
Program name: Arts & Sciences Writing Program

description: Honors in the Major allows students to undertake an intensive project within their major field, culminating in a thesis or creative work and oral defense. Honors in the Major is available in all departments and interdisciplinary programs in the College of Arts & Sciences that offer majors. This is a special opportunity for highly motivated students who are interested in pursuing independent research or creative work with a faculty mentor. By undertaking Honors in the Major, you will develop unique skills that will benefit you in graduate school and in your career. You will demonstrate a capacity for high-level independent work, critical thinking, problem-solving, and written and oral communication. You will also have the chance to work closely with a faculty mentor, which can be an invaluable experience for future academic and professional endeavors.
Program name: Honors in the Major

description: Accelerate your academic and career goals by earning both a bachelor’s and a master’s degree in just five years with the CAS Bachelor’s-to-Master’s program. Through this program, you can pursue graduate-level coursework during your senior year, allowing you to graduate with both degrees in less time and at a lower cost than if you were to complete each degree separately. A number of programs across the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities participate in the Bachelor’s-to-Master’s program, enabling you to earn both a BA and an MA, or a BA and an MS, or a BS and an MS. These programs also provide a path for you to take advantage of advanced coursework during your senior year, allowing you to strengthen your research and analytical skills and expand your understanding of a particular discipline. The Bachelor’s-to-Master’s program is open to Boston University undergraduates from the College of Arts & Sciences, the College of Engineering, and the Questrom School of Business.
Program name: Bachelor's-to-Master's Programs

description: Boston University’s accelerated BA & Master of Public Health (MPH) program offers highly motivated undergraduates the opportunity to earn both a bachelor’s degree and a Master of Public Health in just five years. This unique program is designed for students interested in a career in public health who want to gain a deeper understanding of the field and its diverse applications. Students in the program begin taking graduate-level courses in their senior year, building on their undergraduate studies and preparing for advanced practice and leadership roles in public health. The BA & MPH program is a five-year, 158-credit program that combines the comprehensive undergraduate education of a bachelor’s degree with the specialized public health training of an MPH. Students typically complete 128 credits for their bachelor’s degree and 40 credits for their MPH, with 10 of these credits counting toward both degrees. The program is open to students from any undergraduate major at Boston University, providing a flexible pathway for students with diverse academic backgrounds.
Accreditation status: Boston University School of Public Health is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). The accreditation of the School was reaffirmed in 2023 for a seven-year period, extending to July 1, 2030.
Program name: BA-to-MPH

description: Boston University’s College of Arts & Sciences offers programs for undergraduate and graduate students seeking initial licensure as a secondary school teacher in Massachusetts. The programs combine a student’s rigorous study in a content area (e.g., Biology, English, Mathematics, History, a world language, Chemistry, or Physics) with professional education courses and extensive field experiences. Upon successful completion of the program, students are recommended by Boston University for a Provisional License by the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. Because Massachusetts has signed the NASDTEC Interstate Agreement, this license is recognized in many other states. These programs are for students interested in teaching in secondary schools (grades 8-12). Our programs do not lead to a teaching degree, but rather to a teaching license. Undergraduate students may participate in the licensure program concurrently with their major in a relevant content area. Graduate students pursuing licensure may complete this program as part of their studies towards a master’s degree (MA, MAT, MS) at BU, or as a stand-alone program after completing an undergraduate degree (Post-Baccalaureate Licensure Program).
Program name: Educator Licensure

description: For more than 50 years, SEA has offered unique learning experiences that combine oceanographic, environmental, and nautical sciences with maritime history, literature, and policy. Students spend six weeks on shore in Woods Hole, Massachusetts, preparing for their voyage, followed by four to six weeks at sea, during which time they conduct research, study marine ecosystems, and practice nautical science aboard a tall ship. BU students can choose from a range of SEA programs, from a semester-long program at sea to a summer program focusing on topics such as climate and society, marine biodiversity, and sustainability in marine environments.
Program name: Sea Education Association

description:
The Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies, housed in Boston University’s College of Arts & Sciences, provides students with a holistic understanding of global challenges. The Pardee School is committed to creating new knowledge, training future generations of leaders, and advancing human progress worldwide.
The Pardee School has long been a key player in the development of Boston University’s global mission. Founded in 1953 as the Center for International Relations, it became the Department of International Relations in 1968, and in 2014, a generous endowment from Frederick S. Pardee transformed it into a school.
The Pardee School aims to advance human progress through excellence in teaching, research, and policy engagement in global affairs. Faculty teach undergraduate and graduate students to understand and contribute to the resolution of critical challenges facing the world across the broad spectrum of global affairs, including international relations, diplomacy, economic development, global governance, and regional studies.
Program name: The Frederick S. Pardee School of Global Studies

description: Metropolitan College’s Bachelor of Science in Administrative Sciences with a concentration in Management Studies prepares you to be a versatile leader in any organization. Learn to identify and analyze problems, formulate and implement effective solutions, and develop strong communication skills through our rigorous curriculum. Whether you are seeking a first bachelor’s degree, changing careers, or advancing your current career, the BS in Administrative Sciences is designed to provide you with an in-depth understanding of the critical elements of business and administration. The curriculum integrates various disciplines, including economics, accounting, finance, marketing, and operations management. Our faculty are practitioners in their fields, bringing real-world experience and expertise to the classroom, ensuring you gain practical, relevant skills applicable to today’s dynamic business environment. The program also offers flexibility, with courses available on campus, online, or a blended format, allowing you to tailor your education to your schedule and learning preferences.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Management Studies

description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Mathematics at Boston University’s Metropolitan College (MET) is designed for students who enjoy mathematical theory and problem-solving, and are interested in pursuing careers that involve mathematical thinking. The program provides a solid foundation for those looking to apply their quantitative skills in scientific and technical fields, and also prepares students for further graduate studies. The Applied Mathematics concentration within the BS in Mathematics provides students with a strong foundation in a specific area of applied mathematics, combining theoretical knowledge with practical skills applicable to various industries. Whether students pursue the general mathematics curriculum or the applied mathematics concentration, they will gain a comprehensive understanding of mathematical concepts and problem-solving techniques and will be prepared for a wide range of career opportunities in diverse fields such as data science, finance, engineering, and research, or for advanced studies in mathematics or related disciplines.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Mathematics

description: The Bachelor of Science in Economics provides a rigorous quantitative approach to the study of economics. It is a good choice for students interested in graduate school in economics or business, or for those planning careers in research, financial economics, or actuarial work. The requirements include both intermediate microeconomics and macroeconomics, econometrics, and courses in mathematics and statistics. Students in the BS program may also concentrate in Math-Economics by fulfilling additional requirements.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Economics

description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Computer Science degree program provides students with a broad and deep foundation in the principles and applications of computer science. Our curriculum emphasizes an understanding of both the theory of computation and the practical art of programming and system design. This degree program is designed for students who desire a strong foundation in computer science and may wish to pursue graduate study in the field or a career in the high-tech industry. The undergraduate curriculum is structured to ensure that students acquire a solid foundation in the core areas of computer science and sufficient breadth of knowledge in the supporting disciplines of mathematics and natural sciences. It allows for flexibility in the choice of electives, enabling students to tailor their program to their specific interests within computer science, such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, software engineering, security, and algorithms.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
